utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dostana and her daughter in law, Mira, with three children. Dostana and Mira, there was Milenja, there was Milka, and other names I don't know. There were fifteen of us women and there were 11 men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's stay --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know the names. I don't know the names.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour I think that is sufficient at this point. I'm much obliged to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: With respect to the women that were in the prison with you, do you remember the condition, the physical condition of any one particular woman? Were they in good health or was -- was any -- did any woman appear to you to be injured?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I would have stopped with "what condition were they in."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree completely with you. Were these women in good shape? What was their condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were in good shape, but they were not close to me. They were from Skelani. They were not my neighbours. Those women are from Skelani. They were healthy, they were able bodied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you recall anything about any one particular woman when she was brought in?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There was a girl, a young woman who was wounded and her mother was with her. The two of them had been captured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you remember their names? This wounded young lady and her mother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Milena and her daughter, Stana,. They were in our room. They were both in prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And do you recall the name of the -- do you recall if the mother of the ten year old was also present, Vesna?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Vesna, and her mother was also Stana, they were the first ones to be let out of our prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. Now, when these women were brought in, you said there was 15 in total. Was there a time that any other women were brought in? Well, I will rephrase. For instance, Stana and Milena, the mother and daughter were they brought in --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They were all brought on one day. The ones that were not wounded, the one that was wounded, they were all brought in on that one day, which was our Serbian new year.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And were any other women brought in, after this, after this group?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Those who were brought on that day were the ones that stayed in the prison and this one was wounded. Stana was her name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And in addition -- other than this group that you mentioned, including Stana, on any other day, did any other women come? Did they bring any other women to the prison, or, excuse me, the police station?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They brought, from Cerska, one woman and they put her among us. They put her in prison. She was brought from Cerska.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you remember her name?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Andja.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Could you tell us how long the women, including yourself, were kept at the police station?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We were there, all of us together, just for one night. And on the 19th, we were taken --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter missed the end of that sentence. On the 19th of January, that was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Nikolic, bear with me for a moment, please. Where were you taken on the 19th of January?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were taken to Srebrenica, to the prison there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mrs. Nikolic, did there come a time that you were taken from the room at the police station and taken elsewhere? Just you yourself.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They didn't take me anywhere. That was when Dostana and I were there. They took us for interrogation and it was just me and Dostana. And then, when the other women came, we were all together and we were not taken anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I would like to ask you about that interrogation -- interrogation, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would ask for this one document to be given a new exhibit. I'm about to use Prosecution's Exhibit 56, but we do have another -- we have a document that requires an exhibit number as well. Now, the witness does not read so I will not be showing it to her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I need to see the document first. I need to see the document first.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We do have copies that we will be handing out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I've lost count of the sequence. Perhaps you can help me, Madam Registrar. 519. So this Prosecution exhibit, which is being tendered today, the 12th of April and which bears ERN number 02075725 as regards the Serbian -- Serbo-Croat version, and 03038171 as regards to the translation into English, is being tendered, received and marked as Prosecution Exhibit P519. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mrs. Nikolic, you said you were interrogated. Do you recall what questions were put to you during the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Should I know? It was four years ago. How could I remember?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, do you recall if they asked you personal information, such as -- personal information about yourself and your family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think I want to make sure there is no confusion here. Because I heard you say "it was four years ago", Madam Nikolic. It's not the interview that you had with that English-speaking lady and the interpreter that we are referring to. We are referring to, when you were in Srebrenica, you were taken from the police station to the prison in Srebrenica and you were interrogated there, on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness did say 12 years ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because the transcript says "four years ago". So, we will try to refresh a little bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were interrogating me. They asked me about how things were. I don't know what they asked me. It was a long time ago. I forgot. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. If we tried to refresh your memory a bit, do you think it would help you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They asked me in Srebrenica, one said, "Where were you imprisoned? Where were you captured?" And they also asked me about the cattle. I don't know what else they asked me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you recall if they asked you about your husband?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They asked me questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: What did you think at the time --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They asked me where he was and I said, "I don't know whether he is alive, whether he was killed. I don't know."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic. One moment. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said "He has remained up there" and this has not entered the record. In addition to having said "I don't know whether he is alive or whether he was killed", she also said "He has remained up there." But this has not entered in the transcript, and I just wanted to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. If I hear nothing contradicting that, I take it that it is so, and it will be entered into the record as such. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: At the time of the interrogation, were you aware if your husband was alive or not? Or was he dead? Did you know?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the interest of time I will just ask that these -- well, the second document, Prosecution Exhibit 519, be entered into evidence. I will not read them out to the witness. I think that is as much use as I will use of it -- make of it today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I would like to take you back to the interrogation just briefly. Could you tell us whether or not -- how many people were present during the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When they were interrogating me?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When they were interrogating me, there was just one. When I went for interrogation from the prison, I was taken to the town, there was one who interrogated me and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you recall what this individual was wearing, and were you interrogated by a man or a woman?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It was a man in a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And who escorted you to the interrogation? How were you taken from the police station to the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There was one man who escorted me, who handed me over to the man who interrogated me, and then this first man brought me back to the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: This man that brought you back to the prison, how was he dressed? What type of clothing?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: He had a uniform, a field uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And did you notice if he had a weapon?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, I would like to bring your attention to the time that you were transferred, you along with the other women to -- the time that you were taken from the police station. Do you recall that day?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Of course I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And who took you from the police station to the other building? Who escorted you?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Soldiers did. One was going in front without weapons, and two were behind us. We were some 15 women. We were taken to prison. And one was walking in front of us without weapons, and two were behind us with weapons, when they were taking us to the prison in town.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Were these the same soldiers who brought you to Srebrenica or were these different soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I guess it was the same troops. They had military clothes on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: By that I mean their faces. Did you recognise them as the same people, the same soldiers who had brought you to Srebrenica or were these different men in uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: How did you get from the police station to the other building? Did you walk or were you driven?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We walked all the way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: From the police station up to the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And what building did they take you to, if any?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It was a big building and we were downstairs on the ground floor, and up on the first floor they kept their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: When you were walking -- could you describe this building for us, when you first walked in. Could you describe the layout of it?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: So the room had a floor. It was comfortable. It was like a prison, and there was also the men's prison in that building, and there was the duty officer's room too.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: The room that the women were brought -- all the women were taken to one room; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, all of the women and children.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Could you tell us what was contained in this room?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, there was a bench, nothing else, and there was also a stove, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you recall if there was a window?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There were two small windows.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the temperature was in this room?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, you know it was January. You know how cold it gets. When we have field wood, then we start a fire to warm ourselves and when we don't, then we don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: How were you able to get wood?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How we obtained wood? Well, if they brought us wood, then we would start a fire, and if we didn't get any, then not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Were there any beds in this room?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And where did you --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Just one bench and a stove, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Where did you and the other women sleep?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: On the floor. We had a blanket each and we slept on the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And during the time that you were held in this prison, was food provided to you and water?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We received food once a day. And water? Well, when there was someone to bring it to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: What type of food did you receive?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: From the first till the last day, we got white beans and bread.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Were you permitted to use the toilet, you and the other women?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They said to us that we should knock on the door when in need, and that they would open, because the duty officer was on -- to the right of our room.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you recall how the duty officer was dressed?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: He was wearing civilian clothes, the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Was it always the same duty officer? Or did this person change over the length of time that you were held there?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They were different persons. They changed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And were they always dressed in civilian clothing? Or did their clothing differ from time to time?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It was different. Some of them were in civilian clothes; others in military clothes. It changed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you recall whether they carried weapons?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. I haven't seen any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: You testified a few minutes ago that there were male -- there were eleven male prisoners. Could you tell us, first of all, how it was that you learned that there were male prisoners in the same building with you?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Oh, there were male prisoners, only in another room.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And do you know where, in relation to your room, this room was located? In other words, was it next door or was it across from you? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There is a hallway going through all the building, and on this side there was the duty officer and our room, and next to that there was the men's room.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just one matter. I was just looking at the transcript and my learned friend referred to this witness testifying there we're 11 male prisoners. It may not be a big point, but I searched transcript and I don't see where the witness ever said 11 male prisoners. It's a matter which should be brought to Your Honours' attention.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand, but I distinctly remember that being said. I can't find it at this time in the transcript - -

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I remember hearing it as well, but if necessary we will check. Did you check under 11, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what I looked for.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have done a search as well. It appears in the transcript that the first mention of 11 was when I made reference to it. However, I don't think it is my imagination that it was said. My colleague has confirmed that it was said and it's possible that it simply did not make it into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I imagine that you had searched under "11", so I am searching under "men". Yes, if you look at page 46, line 9, of course you won't find "11" there, but I am sure that you will all agree with me that what is spelled "LEFRN" basically is 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My apologies, that could be the explanation. I can't think of any words which would approximate to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I searched under something different from what I anticipated you would be searching. So let's proceed. Thank you for pointing that out, Mr. Jones, and for your cooperation, Madam Richardson and Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mrs. Nikolic, could you tell us how it was that you became aware that there were male prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How I became aware of it? Well, when they took us there, they were also taken there, and I knew that that's how many there were, that 11 had been captured. They were brought there on the same day as we.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And were you -- did you know any of the male prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, except for Ratko Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And did you see Ratko Nikolic during the time that you were in the prison?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Could you tell us about that. When did you see him? What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I saw him bring us fuel wood and he said to us, "There, ladies, there's some wood for you." And some three people were standing in the door with weapons and he brought us wood.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you remember what condition he was in, what physical condition he was in?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know. How should I know?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, were you able to see his face?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He was -- he had an injury on the face, on the cheek.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: When you say "an injury", what -- could you tell us a little bit more? Could you describe what kind of injury, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There is nothing much to remember. He brought us wood and he was -- well, bloody on the cheeks and scratched and he was taken back to the other room.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And with respect to the room where the men were kept, what, if anything, did you hear during the period of time that you were in this prison? Were you able to hear anything coming from that room?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, what was there to hear? I heard them screaming "Yoy", I don't know why. Of course I didn't know what was going on. I didn't know who was beating them. Ratko knows.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: How often did you hear them screaming? Was it on a daily basis or --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will rephrase the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think it is an objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sometimes they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not an objection, Your Honours. The witness is saying something quite different from what is being interpreted. I heard the witness say she -- that she heard people crying out "Yoy" and it was interpreted differently from what it means in our language. This keeps repeating itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Nikolic, you've heard what Madam Vidovic has just stated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you agree with what she has just said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. For example, why should I talk to you why I moaned? I may have moaned for some reason too. I don't know why people moaned, for what reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I suggest that the question be put to the witness again, so that there is no misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think you need to put the question again and we'll hear her answer. And I would also like to have an explanation of what this "Yoy" means.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mrs. Nikolic, what you were able to hear coming from the room where the male prisoners were kept, could you tell us again what it was that you heard, the types of sounds that you heard.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I heard, for example, people moaning and heard that they were beaten up, but what else should I know about that? I heard them moan sometimes. They were certainly being beaten up, they didn't moan for no reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And how often did you hear this?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How often? Well, sometimes you could hear it, sometimes not. Depending on who would -- who would come there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Was this on a daily basis, or not?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How should I know?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did you hear it more than once?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I heard it two or three times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, to the question, Did you hear it every day, the witness replied, Not every day, how could I have heard it every day. But this wasn't entered in the transcript. I'm not talking to you, witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Nikolic, try to answer me this time. You were asked, a short while ago, the following question: How often did you hear this moaning, and you said -- how often did you hear this, and you said: How often? Well, sometimes you could hear it, sometimes not. Depending on who would -- who would come. Then Madam Richardson asked you again: Was this on a daily basis, or not? Could you repeat your answer to that question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the cries are concerned, they were beaten up. I don't know which troops beat them up, but I heard moans. But I can't tell you everything at the time. They were certainly beaten up, the men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But how many times did you hear the moaning? Did you hear it on a daily basis? Was it every day or was it sporadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not every day, but sometimes. So they weren't -- they weren't beaten every day, but sometimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, back to you. There is another -- I had noticed it actually, it's -- I am sure that this will be corrected later on, at one time the witness said "Ratko knows" and instead we have "Brat" something else. It is page 58, line 12. Thank you. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mrs. Nikolic, you used the term in your testimony "Yo", at least that is how --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "Yoy".

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: "Yoy" in your language, could you just tell us what that means?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It has to be. So when you beat someone, the one beaten says "Yoy", what else should they say?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's enough, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, indeed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Proceed with your next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did you hear the moaning during the day or during the evening, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We didn't hear it at night, sometimes in the daytime.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, I would just like to turn your attention to the treatment of the women in the prison, and if you could tell us how the women were treated during the time that you were in the prison.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They were mistreating the women with knives, with rifles, they were mistreating them as women.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Let's take the first example you gave us, with respect to the knives. Could you tell us exactly what happened with respect to how the women were treated, and you just made reference to knives. Could you recall what happened specifically?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It happened, for example, they would come and someone would put a pistol against you or your body, or a rifle, or a knife. But you have to keep quiet, what could you do?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And how -- I will rephrase the question. When you say "someone would put a pistol against you", did they say anything as they were doing this? And do you recall who did this to you, and how the person was dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are having a problem hearing the witness, especially the first part of her answer. If the technicians could be asked to remedy that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank the interpreters. I imagined so, frankly. Let's do two things. Usher, I don't know if it is possible to bring the -- either the witness nearer to the microphones or the microphones nearer to the witness and lower them a little bit, please, yes. I think that should do the trick. The other thing is this: Madam Nikolic, I can tell you that you have been extremely cooperative and I do appreciate that you have been sitting there for a long time and that, in this process, you tend to get tired. We are trying to do this here, your testimony, as quickly as we can so that we can send you home, and we are trying to do our utmost to make you feel comfortable. There is just one little problem that I see and that is that sometimes, probably because you are tired, you are not speaking loud enough for the interpreters to hear what you are saying. You see now that I have tried to move the microphones nearer to you. What I would like you to do now is to raise your voice a little bit more while you are giving your answers, and that will make the task of the interpreters, which is already difficult in itself, a little bit lighter. All right? Yes. I think you can move to the next question. And I think you need to repeat the question, basically, I mean, because the interpreters didn't catch the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. I will, Your Honour, I will repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mrs. Nikolic, you mentioned an incident with -- or it could have been on more than one occasion. Please tell us, what happened with respect to the women and someone coming to the cell with a knife? Could you tell us -- give us a little bit more detail about when this occurred and what happened exactly.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It wasn't once, it was several times. They would take a knife. They would bring it up to your ears and then throw it into the floor, and then take up the knife again, brings up to -- bring it up to your ear again. And it happened several times.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did they say anything as this was being done? Did they say anything to you or the other women?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They did that to everybody in the room where we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And you said there was another incident with a pistol. I believe that is the word you used. Correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Could you tell us what happened during that particular incident, and if anything was said?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: He took a pistol and put it against my forehead. I was quiet. And he said, "I'll kill you" and then I said, "Well, kill me. What can I do?" And all the while, he was pressing his pistol against my forehead.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Were there any other incidents where you were threatened yourself, either personally or the other women that you recall?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. There were no other women anywhere but in that room.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. And --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you recall if they were wearing uniforms, the individuals who would come into the room with knives and the pistol?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What would they be wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They had shirts and trousers. That was the clothes they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And was this civilian clothing or military clothing?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Military clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I would like to move to another subject matter, and this is with respect to any visitors that you may have had during the time. When I say "you", I mean the women in the cell, yourself and the other women that were held in the cell. Do you recall if anyone visited you during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We were visited. Zulfo came to our house, and Krdza, to ask us where we were going, what we were doing there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. Let's take it one by one. When you say "Zulfo", who is Zulfo? And did you know Zulfo prior to his visiting the cell?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't know him until the moment I was captured. And Zulfo was a good man. He came to ask us what we were doing. He called us "nannies", and Krdza also came.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. We will deal with Krdza in a moment. But with respect to Zulfo, you said you didn't know him. How did you know his name was Zulfo?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't know him until I was put in prison. That's when I saw him. That's when I heard him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Had you seen him prior to this? Did you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. When you say you didn't know him, to be --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't know him. I didn't know him at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. What, if anything, did you learn about Zulfo?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I did not ask any questions. I didn't know anything about him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Who -- if you could listen to my question very carefully. You said the person -- Zulfo visited you.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: How did you know the person --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: He did come and visit us. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. How did you know his name was Zulfo?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I heard it from his soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you know his last name?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know his last name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you remember what he looked like? Could you give us a description of him?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: He was big. Not tall. He was a big man, a heavily-built man.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did Zulfo say anything to you personally during the time he visited?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, not to me personally. He just called us "grannies" and asked us what we were doing, and how we were, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did he ask you anything else?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know that he asked us anything. No, he did not ask us anything. He just said a few words to us, and left.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did he ask you -- if you could just think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, the witness was asked, "Did he ask you anything else?" and she said, "No. I don't know that he asked us anything." So I would object to my learned friend suggesting something which he might have asked her when she's clearly answered that she doesn't know -- that he didn't say anything else, or that she certainly doesn't recall him saying anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's hear the question first and then we will decide whether to take your objection, or whether we will proceed. But I am sure you have understood exactly the -- Mr. Jones' objection --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- which is certainly a very valid one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. A pertinent one. Whether it is valid or not depends on what your question is going to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I would like to -- I would like you, Mrs. Nikolic, to think Zulfo Tursunovic and his visit to the prison?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: She never said it was Zulfo Tursunovic. In fact, we had evidence of another Zulfo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're 100 per cent right, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologize, that was certainly not intentional.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: You mentioned Zulfo visited you at the prison. Please think back to the number of times -- well, I will rephrase the question. How many times did he visit?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Several times.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: The first time he visited, what, if anything, did he say?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: He did not say much. He just asked us what we were doing, how we were. He called us grannies. He did not ask us any questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did you say anything to him?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I just jokingly asked him, Commander, why I am here? And he said, I was confined for 14 years, and you can't be confined for two months? And he says -- and then I said, I don't know why you were confined. I don't know why I am confined. And he says, Well, I was confined for 14 years, and he just laughed. It was said jokingly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did you know what he was referring to, this confinement for 14 years? Did you know what he was talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How should I know? I don't know what he was talking about. I don't know when this was. And it was -- all this happened 12 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: The next time Zulfo visited, do you recall what, if anything, he said to you or the other women in the prison?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Nobody offended him. Nobody told him anything bad to offend him, none of us did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: You stated -- you testified previously that he asked how you were doing. What did you or the other women tell him?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We said we were all right. What else could we have said to him when he asked us how we were?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did he ask about the welfare of anyone else, how anyone else was doing?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How do I know? How should I know that? He came to the women's room and sometimes he would go to the men's room. He was a good man. He was a good man and he treated us well and he behaved well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: After he went -- you testified that he would go to the men's room. Did he ask you - when I say "you", you or the other women - anything after visiting the men's room?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: He went to the men's room and when he came back from that room he talked to us. And he says, What happened? All the men have been killed. And we didn't know. That's what he told us when he came back from the men's room.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure whether the witness said killed or beaten.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And after that, when he told us that, the men were not beaten again. This is the only thing that he told us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mrs. Nikolic, just for clarification, when Zulfo -- after he visited the men's room, what did he ask you and the other women about the men?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: He asked, how come that all the men had been beaten.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter believes that the witness said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we said, we don't know how this came about.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this is a good time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Madam Nikolic, we are going to have another 30-minute break and then it will be a short session and you will go home. In fact, I think it -- I mean, putting myself in your shoes, my cross-examination would last very little, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I don't think I can.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I go home now? Can I go home?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, not yet. I will soon send you home. Don't worry.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I don't think I can undertake to finish today when Ms. Richardson, my learned friend, has not finished her examination-in- chief. That would leave me with something in the range of, I don't know, 15 minutes or something. I can't undertake to finish in 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, the position is as follows: What happens tomorrow? Because this lady will be here for a very short while more. I mean it's ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I apologize, Your Honour. I believe I can certainly try to finish with this witness in the next 10 or 15 minutes tops after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, let's see. And what happens tomorrow? Is the other witness here?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I misunderstood your question, Your Honour. We're not prepared to go forward with the other witness tomorrow. Unfortunately, he could not be brought here in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's have a break. Madam Nikolic, I will give you 30 minutes break now so that you rest, and then we will do our utmost to see if we can finish.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If we can't finish today, you will be here a little bit more tomorrow, and then you can go. Thank you. 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mrs. Nikolic, before the break, you testified that Krdza also visited in addition to Zulfo. Could you tell us about his visits, tell us how often he visited, and what was generally the conversation that he had with the women and yourself.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: He did not come once, he came several times, and he spoke to us nicely, just like the other, Zulfo. He was nice to us and he did not come only once, he came several times. He was a nice man. He did not ill treat us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did there come a time that you were -- I will rephrase the question. Did there come a time that the women that were held with you were released?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were all released on one day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you remember that day? What day it was? Or the month?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I think that it was on the 7th of February.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Now, prior to that day when you were exchanged, did there -- prior to that day, were any of the other women that were held with you --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We were exchanged. No women stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I understand that. But prior to the women being exchanged, was there ever a period of time that other women, including the little girl, were released, or left the cell?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the girl called Sandra or to the girl Stana who was wounded? This is what I'm asking you now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's take it one step at a time. Was Stana released with you, the one who was wounded?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Were any -- you mentioned another name, that other person. Was she released with you?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Was the little girl released with you?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No women were left behind when we were released. There were 21 of us who were released on that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. But before that day, did the little girl leave the prison?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. But Sandra did not leave the prison. She was always with her mother. She always clung to her mother.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And were -- the little girl and her mother, were they exchanged on the exact same day you were? Or did they leave before?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They were all exchanged. Stana and her mother, they left before us, a day. And then Sandra and her mother, they left before as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. Could you tell us about that? How was it that they left before, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know why they left. I can't tell you. I can't tell you why they were let go. I believe that they left some seven days before us. They were released.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Did anyone come to -- during -- excuse me, I will rephrase the question. When they were released, did anyone come to the cell and make any --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's getting very leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will rephrase. I'll do this another way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: You mentioned that the little girl and her mother left before.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, before.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you know why those two left before you and the other women?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They left, the two of them, to be exchanged for two soldiers. And this little girl would be free to go to Skelani, and in Skelani she was to hand over a piece of paper that they gave her and she was to be exchanged for two soldiers. That's why they were released before us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And the little boy, Branko, was he released with you, or before?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Branko stayed with us. He was released with us. His mother came to Skelani, she took him over, and then she took him away.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Was Branko's -- I will rephrase. Branko's relative, I believe you may have testified that his grandmother was in the prison with you.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, she was, but his grandmother went to Skelani as a courier and she never returned. And that's why Branko stayed with us, on his own.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: On these two occasions when Branko's grandmother left and the little girl and her mother left, did anyone come to the prison cell to talk about why they were leaving?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Again, it's a very leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If my learned friend wants to ask if any other people ever visited the cell, in fact, that question has been asked and she answered Zulfo and Krdza. She didn't mention anyone else. But if there is to be an open question as to whether she recalls anyone else visiting the cell, but to put the exact circumstances in which someone might have come, is suggesting to the witness that she's to remember a specific incident. I'd prefer if it could be put in a completely non-leading manner. I think we know what it is about and it is very important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And at this stage particularly, in anticipation of what you are going to ask and all of the information that you are seeking, definitely, Mr. Jones is right. You need to rephrase it in a way that is definitely not leading.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I will rephrase it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you recall Branko's mother -- grandmother, excuse me, leaving? You said she left.

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I do recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you remember the circumstances or whether or not -- I will rephrase the question again. Do you recall whether any information --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: She left as a courier, Branko's grandmother that is. She was supposed to take mail to Skelani, their mail to Skelani, and she was supposed to return, but she never returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: My question, Mrs. Nikolic, is whether or not someone told her, as far as you know, what to do with respect to the mail. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The one who sent her knows why he sent her.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And the person who sent her, do you recall who that was and how this person -- and if this person came to the cell and how he was dressed?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: The person that sent her, did he come to the cell, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I remember. He was in a military uniform. He brought a letter. He told her to go to Skelani to take that letter to Skelani and come back, but she never did. She never came back.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: All right. How did you come to learn about -- I will bring you now to the subject matter of your own exchange and the exchange of the other women in February. How did you come to learn about your exchange?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We learned on Friday when our names were listed, all the prisoners were listed, and then they went to Skelani in order to arrange for an exchange that was supposed to take place there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And who told you you were going to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Krdza told us, he told us, and a soldier of his. He told us, Grandmothers, you will be going home. Our men and their men were today in Skelani together.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And this -- excuse me. And this Krdza, do you recall if, during the times he visited and in addition to the time he talked about the exchange, whether he was dressed in military clothing or in civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Military clothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And who was it that listed your names?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They had Serbian names. I don't know what his name was, but they called him Buda. He made a list of our names on Friday, and on Saturday the exchange took place. He took that list of names to Skelani and we were exchanged in Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And do you know -- excuse me, were there any men exchanged along with yourself on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, three.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you know the names of these men, or were they familiar to you at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't. They were from Skelani, and I don't know any of their names.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you recall what their appearance, their physical condition was?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The men? They were -- the three of them? They were heavily beaten up, the three of them, all the three of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And who took you and -- yourself and the other women, including these three men, and the three men, to the exchange? How did you get there? And who escorted you?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There was a van from Srebrenica. A van took us from Srebrenica to the exchange, from the prison in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Now, I just have a couple of other questions for you. With regard to your home, could you tell us if you ever received any compensation for the damage to your home?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We never received anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Was it just your house that was burned, or did any other structure burn as well?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: My house was burnt, but no other house was left -- was spared in the village. Only the house of Rado Nikolic, which had not been finished, remained standing. Everything else had been burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And this is with respect to all of the houses, the 25 houses in Popovici?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Nikolic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Richardson. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I think I can -- I can certainly start now. I'm not sure if I will finish --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have I finished?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: -- because I might need to show some photographs, which will take time to organise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Take your time, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If you will give me a moment just to get the lectern on the desk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Now, Madam Nikolic, Mr. Jones is going to start with his questions. You probably have heard what he said. He will do his best to try and finish today, if he can. But it may be a little bit difficult which would mean that you will go to the hotel, have a rest, return tomorrow afternoon and we will finish in a few minutes and then we can send you home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean I can go home tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, if they can arrange for your transportation tomorrow, you can definitely go home tomorrow. Yes, it will be in the afternoon. I mean probably it will be Wednesday. I don't know if there are any flights tomorrow -- tomorrow evening out of Amsterdam to where you live. But I can assure you, Madam Nikolic, that our staff will do their utmost to return you home at the earliest possible time. In any case, I wish to confirm to you, I'm confirming to you that tomorrow, within a few minutes after we start, you will be finished. Mr. Jones, you do have a cross-examination, in other words?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, all right. Then let's start.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. I will try to make [Realtime transcript read in error "fake"] it as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic, first of all, I need to ask you a few more questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. This, I will not accept, Mr. Jones, say it -- okay, they have changed it because the transcript said "I will try to fake it as quickly as I can."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That could be misconstrued in all sorts of way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So please don't fake it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I will be nothing but genuine.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic, firstly, I need to ask you a few more questions about Mandici and Kravica and what you saw on the 7th and 8th of January. Now, first, I'm not sure if you told us how far Mandici is from Popovici. Can you just tell us how long it would take by foot to get to Mandici from Popovici?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And in Mandici, are all the houses on the hill or just some of them?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. All of them are on the hill. They can be seen from our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. And I think you told us you saw houses in Mandici burning on the 7th of January, 1993. You didn't see who, if anyone, set fire to those houses, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We saw the houses burning, and the people from Mandici who were in our village with us also watched. We saw all the houses burning, but I don't know who set fire to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. And you didn't actually see someone physically setting fire to houses in Mandici, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't even see it in my village, let alone in Mandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. You mentioned how cows were taken from, I think you said, two households in Mandici. What, in fact, are we talking about? Was there three or four cows?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just so we know, how many?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Two oxen and cows were driven away. They belonged to Obramovic and Risto. It was at 5 p.m. when the cattle was driven away and the village was burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. And again, you don't know, do you, who drove the cattle away?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How should we have known?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, as far as Kravica is concerned, Kravica is in fact a large village, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Kravica is in the valley. It is not on a hill. It's in the valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And it comprises many houses spread over a large area. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. In Kravica there were many houses along the road, on various sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Now, you've told us you didn't see Kravica on the 7th of January, 1993, but you passed through on the 8th of January. Now, when you passed --

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I passed there on the 8th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. And you're not saying, are you, that you saw all the houses in Kravica and that you saw that every single one of them had been burnt to the ground, are you?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Nothing was standing in Kravica when I passed there on January 8th.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But you saw only a part of Kravica, would you agree? In other words you didn't see every house in Kravica that day, did you? You saw a portion of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We did see a portion of Kravica, the part of the village where we went through. But there were other houses in Kravica also, but we couldn't see them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Can you give us a rough estimate of how many damaged houses you saw? How many houses were damaged by fire on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I couldn't tell you how many were damaged. I wasn't there to see troops burning houses. I saw -- I just saw houses burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But did you see houses burning? Or you saw some houses which had burnt down?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I saw my house burn. And when I entered the house, it was all in flames, from the ground floor to the roof. And all the houses burned like mine and I watched my house burn.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Nikolic, I'm not going to dwell on this but we're talking about Kravica now, the village of Kravica. And are you saying that you saw every single house in Kravica burnt to the ground? Or are you saying that you saw some houses in Kravica which had been damaged by fire?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We passed Kravica, and I saw everything and the part of the village that we went through. And certainly, the other part of the village wouldn't have been spared if they burnt this one, they must have burnt the other one also.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, we don't want you to make assumptions, Ms. Nikolic, or to speculate. We only want to know what you yourself saw. So I take it from your answer that you saw part of the village, but you didn't see the other part of Kravica? In other words, the part you went through is all you saw?

utterances.speaker: MILOSAVA NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm going to have to return to the subject with some photographs of Kravica tomorrow, just to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, if -- we were discussing, Judge Eser and myself, a short while ago, and I explained that once you start the cross- examination, we usually avoid interrupting you and we let you go, obviously because that's how it should be. But if it is convenient for you to stop at this stage, we would give the opportunity to the witness to go to the hotel a little bit earlier. Tomorrow she is going to be in the witness box, it seems, for a while, not too long. And we shall be 20 minutes later tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I think this is a very sensible suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it is better and we'll stop now and we will send her home.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. That's an excellent idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Madam Nikolic, if you prefer to take the next 20 minutes and finish what you need to finish today, you can --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine. I think there is no need to fatigue the witness any further today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I sense that she is tired and she is getting tired by the hour, you know, or by the minute. So, Madam Nikolic, we are going to stop here today so that you can go to your hotel and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- have dinner and rest. Tomorrow, we will start at 2.15 here and I reckon that you will be testifying for a very short while. So in the meantime, if it is at all possible to make arrangements to have her transferred over tomorrow, then go ahead. If not, then we will still give her an opportunity to stay here, very little tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. We will contact the Victims and Witnesses Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Obviously it doesn't depend on you. All right. Thank you. We stand adjourned until tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 13th day of 23 April, 2005 at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.45 p.m.,
